arxiv-1802-08555.title: PHASE TRANSITION IN S ​ U ​ ( N ) × U ⁡ ( 1 ) SU(N)\times U(1) GAUGE THEORY WITH MANY FUNDAMENTAL BOSONS
arxiv-1802-08555.creator: Ankur Das University of Kentucky email ada258@g.uky.edu
arxiv-1802-08555.description: Abstract Here we study the Renormalization group flow of S ​ U ​ ( N ) × U ⁡ ( 1 ) SU(N)\times U(1) gauge theory with M M -fundamental bosons in 4 − ϵ 4-\epsilon dimension by calculating the beta functions.

arxiv-2005-12819.title: Density of arithmetic representations of function fields
arxiv-2005-12819.creator: Hélène Esnault, Moritz Kerz
arxiv-2005-12819.description: Abstract Abstract. We propose a conjecture on the density of arithmetic points in the deformation space of representations of the étale fundamental group in positive characteristic. This conjecture has applications to étale cohomology theory, for example it implies a Hard Lefschetz conjecture. We prove the density conjecture in tame degree two for the curve {\mathbb P}^{1}\setminus\{0,1,\infty\} . Keywords.

arxiv-2103-14678.title: Generating optical supercontinuum and frequency comb in tenuous plasmas
arxiv-2103-14678.creator: Kenan Qu, Nathaniel J. Fisch
arxiv-2103-14678.description: Abstract There are several mechanisms by which the frequency spectrum of a laser broadens when it propagates at near-relativistic-intensity in tenuous plasma. Focusing on one dimensional effects, we identify two strong optical nonlinearities, namely, four-wave mixing (FWM) and forward Raman scattering (FRS), for creating octave-wide spectra.

arxiv-2307-10377.title: Spontaneous orbital polarization in the nematic phase of FeSe
arxiv-2307-10377.creator: Connor A. Occhialini, Joshua J. Sanchez, Qian Song, Gilberto Fabbris, Yongseong Choi, Jong-Woo Kim, Philip J. Ryan, Riccardo Comin
arxiv-2307-10377.description: Abstract Abstract The origin of nematicity in FeSe remains a critical outstanding question towards understanding unconventional superconductivity in proximity to nematic order. To understand what drives the nematicity, it is essential to determine which electronic degree of freedom admits a spontaneous order parameter independent from the structural distortion.

arxiv-2503-00338.title: Long-Term Timing Analysis of PSR J1741 − - 3016: Efficient Noise Characterization Using PINT
arxiv-2503-00338.creator: Yirong Wen, Jingbo Wang *, Wenming Yan *, Jianping Yuan, Na Wang, Yong Xia, Jing Zou
arxiv-2503-00338.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Yirong Wen, Jingbo Wang *, Wenming Yan *, Jianping Yuan, Na Wang, Yong Xia, Jing Zou. The stable rotation of young pulsars is often interrupted by two non-deterministic phenomena: glitches and red timing noise. Timing noise provides insights into plasma and nuclear physics under extreme conditions. The framework leverages rotational symmetry in pulsar spin-down models and temporal symmetry in noise processes to achieve computational efficiency, aligning with the journal’s focus on symmetry principles in physical systems.

arxiv-2510-12135.title: Coexistence of Spectrally Stable and Unstable Modes in Black Hole Ringdowns
arxiv-2510-12135.creator: Peng Wang a, Tianshu Wu b,a
arxiv-2510-12135.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Peng Wang a, Tianshu Wu b,a. Recent studies have shown that a secondary potential barrier, forming a potential well outside the event horizon, can destabilize the Quasinormal Mode (QNM) spectrum of black holes. We find that spectral instability may persist even after the potential well vanishes, giving rise to a distinct family of spectrally unstable QNMs that differ from the spectrally stable modes localized near the potential peak and associated with the photon sphere.

pmc-10600338.title: The prey of the Harpy Eagle in its last reproductive refuges in the Atlantic Forest
pmc-10600338.creator: Mylena Kaizer, Brener Fabres, Francisca Helena Aguiar-Silva, Tânia Margarete Sanaiotti, Alexandro Ribeiro Dias, Aureo Banhos
pmc-10600338.description: The Harpy Eagle (Harpia harpyja) is threatened with extinction throughout its distribution in the neotropical forests. In the Atlantic Forest, deforestation has reduced the number of suitable habitats, with only a few remnant forest fragments hosting active nests; currently, the only known nests in this region are in the Central Atlantic Forest Ecological Corridor (CAFEC), in Brazil.

pmc-11497359.title: Short-Term Exposure to Foodborne Xenoestrogens Affects Breast Cancer Cell Morphology and Motility Relevant for Metastatic Behavior In Vitro
pmc-11497359.creator: Giorgia Del Favero, Janice Bergen, Lena Palm, Christian Fellinger, Maria Matlaeva, András Szabadi, Ana Sofia Fernandes, Nuno Saraiva, Christian Schröder, Doris Marko
pmc-11497359.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). Breast cancer is highly susceptible to metastasis formation. During the time of disease progression, tumor pathophysiology can be impacted by endogenous factors, like hormonal status, as well as by environmental exposures, such as those related to diet and lifestyle. New lines of evidence point toward a potential role for foodborne endocrine disruptive chemicals in this respect; however, mechanistic understanding remains limited.

pmc-11610349.title: Divergent trends in the incidence and mortality of acute myocardial ischaemic syndrome, especially in women. Evidence from Finland in 1996–2021
pmc-11610349.creator: Atte Kallström, Ida Holopainen, Oleg Kambur, Markus Perola, Veikko Salomaa, Aki S. Havulinna, Markus Ramste, Juha Sinisalo
pmc-11610349.description: ObjectiveAlthough the incidence and case fatality (CF) of acute myocardial ischaemic syndrome (AMIS) have declined in recent decades, some studies have suggested a potential stagnation in this decline. We examined if a similar development in AMIS trends can be observed in Finland from 1996 to 2021 among persons aged 35–74 years.

pmc-12483447.title: Rethinking the strongest link: VAL, ratings, and team success in Hungarian basketball
pmc-12483447.creator: Benedek Ágost Nagy, Botond Ágoston Nagy, Ágoston Nagy, József Gáll, Tamás Sterbenz
pmc-12483447.description: IntroductionThis study evaluates the impact of individual player performance–particularly the VAL rating–on team success in professional basketball. It examines whether basketball operates as a “strong-link” sport, where outcomes depend primarily on top-performing players.MethodsA quantitative analysis was conducted on the 2022/2023 Hungarian NB I/A men's league, using 21 offensive and defensive statistical indicators.

pmc-12511744.title: Pneumococcal Vaccination in Korean Adults: 2025 Recommendations by the Korean Society of Infectious Diseases
pmc-12511744.creator: Joon Young Song, Ki Tae Kwon, Wan Beom Park, Ji Yun Noh, Sun Hee Park, Eun Ju Choo, Min Joo Choi, Jun Yong Choi, Jung Yeon Heo, Won Suk Choi, the Committee of Adult Immunization in the Korean Society of Infectious Diseases
pmc-12511744.description: The 20-valent pneumococcal conjugate vaccine (PCV20) was approved by the Korean Ministry of Food and Drug Safety in October 2024. Despite the ongoing national immunization programs that include pneumococcal conjugate vaccines for children and 23-valent pneumococcal polysaccharide vaccine (PPSV23) for adults, the burden of invasive pneumococcal disease and pneumococcal community-acquired pneumonia remains high among the elderly and high-risk adults.

pmc-12649861.title: Effects of Different Afforestation Measures on Biological Soil Crust Properties and Microbial Communities in an Alpine Sandy Land
pmc-12649861.creator: Shaobo Du, Huichun Xie, Gaosen Zhang, Feng Qiao, Guigong Geng, Chongyi E
pmc-12649861.description: Simple SummaryAlpine sandy areas in the Gonghe Basin, which had been subjected to four afforestation measures, exhibited a gradual increase in water content, nutrient content, enzymatic activities, and bacterial community richness and diversity with succession from the bare sand stage to an algae crust and then to a moss crust.

pmc-12695550.title: Gallic acid alleviates visceral hyperalgesia following maternal separation in mice by inhibiting EphrinB2/EphB2 signaling mediated activation of neurons and glial cells
pmc-12695550.creator: Shu-fen Guo, Yu Wang, Han Zheng, Hong-qin Tu, Yu-qing Xi, Dan Li, Zheng-liang Ma, Wei Zhang, Jia-ping Ruan
pmc-12695550.description: BackgroundEarly life stress (ELS) causes functional gastrointestinal issues linked to visceral hyperalgesia. Activation of spinal neurons and glial cells is key to the development and persistence of visceral hyperalgesia. Our previous research has shown that EphrinB2/EphB2 signaling in the spinal cord facilitates this hyperalgesia through neuron and glial cell activation.

pmc-12703046.title: Dysbiosis and Links of the Middle Ear, Nasal, and Oral Microbiota in Chronic Otitis Media with Effusion
pmc-12703046.creator: Jin Li, Shenglong Xu, Qin Gu, Xuan Sun, Yahan Zhao, Peng Zhang, Yi Li, Yan Zhao, Luo Zhang
pmc-12703046.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). Chronic otitis media with effusion (COME) is a common condition that can lead to hearing loss without acute inflammation. However, its underlying pathogenesis remains poorly understood, particularly with regard to microbial contributions. In this study, we characterized and compared the microbiota of the middle ear, nasal cavity, and oral cavity in 100 patients with COME and 77 controls using 16S rRNA gene sequencing.

pmc-12935579.title: Virtual reality as a distraction technique in pediatric patients undergoing orthopedic procedures: A systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials
pmc-12935579.creator: Abdullah M Alharran, Abdulrahman Emad AlAyyaf, Abdullah Addar, Reggie Hamdy, Yousef Marwan
pmc-12935579.description: Introduction:Pain and anxiety are common in pediatric orthopedic procedures such as cast or pin removal, often leading to distress and physiological stress responses. Virtual reality (VR) offers immersive distraction and has shown promise in pediatric procedural care; however, evidence in orthopedic procedures remains limited.

pmc-13071520.title: Current status and prospects of prenatal ultrasound diagnosis of congenital heart disease in fetuses: a narrative review
pmc-13071520.creator: Hui Xin, Lei Wang, Guifeng Ding, Guilan Ding, Lingqian Meng, Hong’e Wan
pmc-13071520.description: Background and ObjectiveCongenital heart disease (CHD) is the most common congenital anomaly and a leading cause of infant mortality. Fetal echocardiography (FE) serves as the cornerstone of prenatal screening, yet significant heterogeneity exists in its diagnostic performance. This review aims to critically appraise the current status, technological advancements, and persistent challenges in FE for diagnosing CHD.

pmc-13154382.title: Identification of Two Novel Variants in CRYGD and OCRL Genes in the Chinese Population With Hereditary Congenital Cataracts Using Whole Exome Sequencing
pmc-13154382.creator: Jianlong Zhuang, Nan Huang, Yu′e Chen, Haijuan Lou, Junyu Wang, Wanyu Fu, Chunnuan Chen, Harleen Khatra
pmc-13154382.description: BackgroundGenetic variants are the leading cause of congenital cataract (CC). To date, numerous genes have been implicated in the development of CC. The objective of the present study was to report two previously unrecognized gene variants associated with CC in two unrelated Chinese families, identified through whole exome sequencing (WES).MethodsTwo unrelated Chinese families affected by CC were recruited.

pmc-13474732.title: plsMD: a plasmid reconstruction tool from short-read assemblies
pmc-13474732.creator: Maryam Lotfi, Deena Jalal, Ahmed A. Sayed
pmc-13474732.description: BackgroundWhile whole genome sequencing has become a cornerstone of antimicrobial resistance surveillance, the reconstruction of plasmid sequences from short-read data remains a challenge due to repetitive sequences and assembly fragmentation. Current computational tools for plasmid identification and binning have limitations in reconstructing full plasmid sequences, hindering downstream analyses like phylogenetic studies and antimicrobial resistance gene tracking.

uslaw-usc-t49-s24323.title: 49 U.S.C. § 24323 — Prohibition on smoking on Amtrak trains
uslaw-usc-t49-s24323.creator: United States Congress
uslaw-usc-t49-s24323.description: United States Code, Title 49 (Transportation); Part C (Passenger Transportation); Chapter 243 (Amtrak). Current through Public Law 119-134, as published by the Office of the Law Revision Counsel. (a) Prohibition.— Beginning on the date of enactment of this section, Amtrak shall prohibit smoking, including the use of electronic cigarettes, onboard all Amtrak trains. (b) Electronic Cigarette Defined.— In this section, the term “electronic cigarette” means a device that delivers nicotine or other.
